messages:
SupportBot: FYI — BlueWave reported a sustained p95 latency spike on /v1/generate (model=redwood-long-ctx-4k). Spike started ~2026-03-17T14:02Z. Example req IDs: rw/bluewave/948227, rw/bluewave/948231. Customer says p95 jumped from ~2.2s -> ~6.8s. Logs: https://s3.redwood/bluewave/9482-logs.zip :warning:

Maya: ack, adding to eng-runtime board and paging infra/profiler. @Ryan can you take profiler traces? @Lee can you look at autoscaling/runner state? :eyes:

Ryan: I can. Need a sample request id + payload size. Prefer running perf on canary runner first.

SupportBot: sample attached in the logs: payload tokens ~3200 (mostly system + history). Request id rw/bluewave/948227 has full headers.

Olivia: did we deploy anything last night? PR #3421 touched batching/windowing configs for long-ctx models.

Nate: infra alert showed spike in connections from bluewave org at ~14:00 UTC. Autoscaler log snippet: `scale event skipped: last_scale_ts within cooldown` — looks like scale_up_delay prevented additional replica. Link: https://grafana.redwood/d/infra/autoscaler

Maya: OK. Priorities: 1) reproduce and profile, 2) check autoscaler + runner CPU, 3) short-term mitigation for the customer (fallback policy). Ryan, I'll need a short playbook you can run.

Ryan: Plan: (a) run perf/flamegraph on runner-22 (canary) for RBs hitting that model; (b) collect pprof traces for the model worker; (c) compare kernel time vs. user time. Commands I'll run:

```
# on runner
sudo perf record -F 99 -g -a -- sleep 30
sudo perf script | ./flamegraph.pl > /tmp/bluewave-flame.svg
# for pprof from worker
curl -sS http://worker-22:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30 > /tmp/pprof.pb
pprof --svg /usr/local/bin/inference /tmp/pprof.pb > /tmp/pprof.svg
```

Ryan: I'll also fetch `redwood.api.latency.route.generate.p95` around the window from Grafana.

Lee: Investigating autoscaler now. Current config for that pool: min_replicas=2, max_replicas=20, scale_up_threshold=0.7, scale_up_delay=120s. The traffic from BlueWave is bursty (many long-ctx requests) so batching config might be keeping workers busy longer and preventing quick scale-ups.

Ryan: Initial flamegraph (canary) — big CPU wedge at `kv_cache::lookup` and another significant wedge inside attention kernel (cuda call overhead + kernel retries). Summary lines: `kv_cache::lookup 28%`, `attention_kernel::dispatch 35%`, `io/read_chunks 10%`.

Maya: interesting. kv_cache spike suggests cache miss storm or inefficient locking. Any recent changes to kv cache?

Olivia: PR #3398 modified kv_cache eviction heuristics (merged 3 days ago). It reduced memory but touched lookup path. Could be related.

Nate: infra metrics show runner-22 GPU util ~82% and CPU steal high. Autoscaler didn't add replicas because pending pods had `ImagePullBackOff` earlier (short outage) and cooldown blocked scaling.

Maya: short-term mitigation: (A) route BlueWave to quantized-variant `redwood-long-ctx-4k-q` which uses lower kernel load, (B) temporarily decrease scale_up_delay to 30s for the pool, (C) throttle their concurrency on API key to reduce burst. Thoughts?

Lee: (B) is easy but needs infra-owner signoff. (C) can be done via rate-limit rule in API gateway; I can draft limit rule. (A) requires model alias + canary routing — product already supports per-customer route.

Ryan: I support (A) — quantized variant reduced attention kernel time by ~40% in local benchmarks for similar payloads. I can validate correctness on a small sample and push canary traffic.

Olivia: I'll open a rollback PR for the kv_cache change if profiling continues to implicate it. Created draft PR #3450 (revert kv_cache change) — needs review.

Maya: I'll own customer comms. SupportBot please tell BlueWave we're triaging, will attempt a temporary fallback to quantized-variant and update in 30 minutes.

SupportBot: Updated ticket RW-7231: "Investigating latency for /v1/generate; mitigation path: fallback to quantized variant; infra scaling tweaks; profiling in progress." ETA: 30m. :white_check_mark:

Ryan: Running perf now on canary. If we see kernel retries, I'll capture CUDA logs and escalate to runtime-kernels. Also grabbing `strace` for worker to ensure no syscall stalls.

Lee: I lowered scale_up_delay to 30s for `bluewave-pool` in staging; will promote to prod after Ryan confirms profiler results.

Olivia: PR #3450 opened for review: https://git.redwood/pr/3450 — marking @maya @ryan for review.

Maya: Thanks. Assigning follow-ups: Ryan = profiler + validate quantized fallback; Lee = autoscaler tweak + gateway rate-limit change; Olivia = PR/revert and review; Nate = verify runner health and image issues. I'll sync in 25m.

Ryan: First perf run done. Flamegraph + pprof uploaded: https://artifacts.redwood/bluewave/948227/perf.tar.gz — kv_cache hotspot confirmed, attention kernel also heavy. Next: reproduce on dedicated benchmark to rule out multi-tenant interference.

SupportBot: Customer updated: "Appreciate the quick response — waiting for your update."

Maya: Good progress. Keep thread updates here. If anyone finds a clear culprit (kv cache vs batching), drop a short note. :thumbsup:

Olivia: noted — will push draft revert if Ryan's next run still points to kv_cache.

Nate: I'll follow up on the image pull issue and ensure nodes are healthy for scale-up.

Lee: Once Ryan validates fallback, I'll flip routing for BlueWave and monitor p95.

SupportBot: Next status update scheduled at 1769876743 (in ~5m)"
